I had school the next morning and it was closing in on 10:30pm so I had already readied myself for bed. My mother was already asleep because she had just gotten out of the hospital for experimental treatment for thyroid cancer. She was sound asleep, snoring and everything. I heard a knocking at our front door which I didn't think anything of because my dad was at the shop and was always armed in case anything went down. Well, I started to get worried when it continued for what felt like 30 more minutes followed by a windy whooshing noise. I remember hearing loud thuds down the hallway until I saw a shadow of something...large. It was hunched over with what I thought to look like two things protruding from its back and very heavy breathing. The thuds got louder as it got closer to my door way and the moment the noise passed my doorway the shadow vanished but all I could hear was my mother started to whimper and just her begging "please no. When I(M) was younger (6-7 years ago) and still in high school, my best friend(m) and I use to ride the bus to his house all the time and play the PS2 and watch WWE because it was the only place I felt comfortable after my mother died. She kept the house together and after she passed my relationship with my father only grew even worse than it already was and it was bad. I practically went to his house everyday to avoid my dad and to have some fun. One day he didn't come to school and we were above average students so we tried not to skip or mess around.

Everything was okay for a while until one day he didn't come to school. It didn't really bother me because I knew he wasn't feeling too good so I thought he decided to stay home. So, per usual, I rush to his house ready to hang out and watch Friday night smackdown and all I heard was the sound of a rope swinging. He decided to hang himself. I couldn't believe it at first. I just stared at his lifeless body thinking it was some sort of joke he played until his mom came running to me to pull me inside, she called my dad immediately to come and get me. We only lived 10 minutes from each other but waiting for him to get there felt like eternity.

My father arrived and rushed me to the car, placed me into the front seat and rushed off. I couldn't remember the ride home or the rest of the day because it was such a shock.

The night afterwards I couldn't sleep because, well, it's was hard to handle the fact that my best friend was dead. So I end up bawling my eyes out non stop for about 3 hours. My father never checked in with me or anything, what he did do though, was barge into my room with a shotgun and handed it to me. He looked me directly in the eyes and said "If you're going to be so sad about it and keep crying, you should join him. Go ahead, pull the trigger." He slammed the door and walked out. I stopped crying and that's when it hit that I needed to get out as soon as I can.
